page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and features 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system includes 372.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 3.88 GB per core. Graphics and parallel computing acceleration are provided by four NVIDIA Turing T4 GPUs, delivering a combined 64 GB of VRAM. The instance has a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps and contains no local storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate a significant divergence between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is weak, with a stress-ng score of 1103.89, and single-threaded gzip compression is poor at 19.2 GB/sec. Conversely, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 70574.45 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 287.37 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks is highly efficient at 3924.63 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write speeds remain average. Redis SET operations are highly performant, reaching 64.27 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high resource density for parallel computing and GPU-accelerated workloads, though the lack of local storage requires external storage configurations. The primary tradeoff lies in its low single-core performance compared to its excellent multi-core scaling. It is best suited for workloads that can leverage its four NVIDIA T4 GPUs and massive core count, such as machine learning inference, parallel data processing, multi-threaded decompression, and high-throughput Redis deployments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for parallel processing and machine learning workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor, it features 96 dedicated physical cores, 372.0 GB of RAM, and four NVIDIA Turing T4 GPUs providing 64 GB of total VRAM. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps, though it lacks local storage. Benchmark data highlights a significant tradeoff: single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression are weak, whereas multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded decompression are highly robust, ranking in the top 25%. Additionally, it demonstrates strong performance in Redis SET operations and cached memory bandwidth. This configuration is highly suitable for GPU-accelerated workloads, parallel data processing, and high-throughput database operations.
